cohort: 368 women with singleton, normal to low-risk, term pregnancies who received either midwife-led or obstetrician-led care at a tertiary maternity hospital in Singapore between 2013 and 2014
finding: Midwife-led care was associated with longer total duration of labor and fewer total antenatal visits but showed no significant differences in other birth outcomes compared to obstetrician-led care in low-risk women.
mod_finding: No significant difference in mode of delivery was found between midwife-led and obstetrician-led care groups.
